boundaries.interval: Before status invoke through its response and a subsequent requestAnimationFrame callback.
boundaries.conclusion: Not pure IPC latency: the metric includes frame scheduling. Status checks process-cell presence, not upstream readiness.

boundaries.interval: chat_connect invoke through response, including native supervisor acquisition, mutex acquisition and event binding.
boundaries.conclusion: Native setup already attempts prewarm. Cold process spawn is a fallback if the cell is empty; connect latency alone does not establish that it occurred.

boundaries.clock: No phase durations recorded by these functions
boundaries.interval: Native bridge spawn, Node startup/imports, proxy spawn, initialize response, thread/start response, session.ready emission.
boundaries.conclusion: These are distinct phases without per-phase timing in the inspected functions; no attribution of the measured delay to one phase is justified.

boundaries.interval: chat_replay invoke through response after binding; buffered events can be delivered during replay.
boundaries.conclusion: Receiving session.ready can reflect buffered delivery, not the instant upstream became ready.

boundaries.clock: frontend Date.now at start and receive
boundaries.interval: startAreChatControlPlane call through receipt of session.ready.
boundaries.conclusion: Starts after native setup prewarm; not full cold desktop launch-to-ready. Wall-clock adjustments can affect elapsed time.

boundaries.clock: Node Date.now emission to frontend Date.now projection
boundaries.interval: Oldest batched delta emission through direct textContent update and projection timestamp.
boundaries.conclusion: Cross-process wall-clock subtraction includes delivery and batching. It is not isolated DOM work; no cross-process monotonic origin is established.
missing: separate receive-to-flush and DOM update spans

boundaries.clock: Node Date.now emission to frontend Date.now rAF callback
boundaries.interval: Oldest delta emission through animation-frame callback scheduled after projection.
boundaries.conclusion: A requestAnimationFrame callback is the recorded boundary, not proof of pixels presented. Projection timestamp is taken before conditional scrolling.
missing: actual presentation evidence if required by a future contract

definitions.statement: Frame scheduling may account for more of the handshake measurement than the status IPC round trip.
definitions.mechanism: The existing interval ends after a requestAnimationFrame callback, so main-thread scheduling contributes to its duration.
definitions.falsifier: In a qualified paired campaign, post-status frame wait is no greater than status IPC in most sessions and the controlled scheduling change does not reduce it.
definitions.baseline: Current status invoke plus subsequent frame callback, with additive phase spans.
definitions.treatment: Same instrumentation and status semantics; defer only identified unrelated startup UI work until after the callback.
definitions.prediction: Post-status frame-wait span decreases while status IPC span and status semantics remain stable.
controls: Same window visibility and refresh mode
required_spans: frontend status response to frame callback

definitions.statement: Late prewarm completion or upstream initialization may explain startup delay even when chat_connect itself is short.
definitions.mechanism: Native prewarm, process acquisition, bridge startup, initialize and thread/start are distinct intervals; process presence does not imply readiness.
definitions.falsifier: Correlated qualified sessions show readiness already emitted before binding, with neither prewarm waiting nor upstream initialization on the launch-to-ready critical path; a scheduling-only prewarm change does not improve that path.
definitions.baseline: Current native prewarm placement with process-local spans and launch/session correlation.
definitions.treatment: Move only the prewarm scheduling point earlier without reusing a process from a previous desktop session or changing initialization semantics.
definitions.prediction: Launch-to-visible-ready decreases if prewarm overlap is limiting; if initialization duration dominates unchanged, that alternative remains open.
controls: Fresh desktop and bridge processes in each arm
required_spans: frontend monotonic connect to ready receive
confounders: OS filesystem caches are not reset by a fresh process

definitions.statement: Buffered session.ready delivery may dominate the observed connect-to-ready interval after upstream initialization has finished.
definitions.mechanism: Event binding and replay determine when a previously emitted ready event reaches the frontend.
definitions.falsifier: Correlated qualified traces show ready is never buffered or replay residence is negligible, and changing replay scheduling alone does not reduce visible-ready latency.
definitions.baseline: Existing event bind and replay order with ready-event identity and native buffer-residence spans.
definitions.treatment: Prioritize replay immediately after binding, preserving event ordering, deduplication and delivery semantics.
definitions.prediction: Native buffer residence and frontend ready-receive delay decrease without reducing upstream initialization duration.
controls: Same ready-event identity across emission, buffering and receipt
required_spans: ready event correlation ID and replay flag

definitions.statement: Frontend batching and conditional scrolling may explain delta-to-frame delay independently of upstream delta production.
definitions.mechanism: The oldest batched delta anchors the metric, projection is timestamped before scrolling, and paint ends at a frame callback rather than presented pixels.
definitions.falsifier: Qualified correlated spans show batching, DOM update and scrolling are small relative to delivery, and coalescing redundant scroll operations does not improve receive-to-frame timing.
definitions.baseline: Current batching, DOM update and conditional scrolling with additive frontend spans.
definitions.treatment: Coalesce redundant scroll operations within each existing batch while preserving text order and user scroll intent.
definitions.prediction: Scroll cost and frontend receive-to-frame decrease without changing content, delta ordering or existing metric definitions.
controls: Same replayable delta stream and essay length
Same viewport and user scroll position
Separate provider runs from deterministic delivery fixtures
confounders: Frame callback is not pixel presentation
